cells.tense: The pull is here and you are meeting it with your eyes open.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you are drawn toward, today, and say what you will keep doing about it — out loud, in your own words.
cells.core: A direction is showing, and you are not fighting it. When something genuinely lands, you can say yes to it and still be standing where you were. The orienting is clean — you are pointed at something you would choose again.\n\nNothing is being forced. You move with the pull instead of performing it, and you are not spending energy shrinking it or inflating it. Steady attention holds this, not pressure — the way you would look after anything you chose deliberately. What you are drawn toward and what you are doing point the same way, and that agreement saves you work in small moments you probably do not stop to count.
cells.sheetLine: You are pointed at something real and you are moving with it.
cells.verb: meeting one stream and choosing to flow with it
cells.place: standing where the pull toward what you actually want is felt

cells.tense: You are already living in the version of this where it worked out, and you are hauling everyone toward it before it has happened.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you are pushing forward and leave it alone for a day — let it arrive at its own speed.
cells.core: The pull is strong and you are running ahead of it, trying to land the whole thing before it has had time to become real. Conversations turn into recruitment. You talk about the future as though it were already settled and ask people to meet you there.\n\nThe connection you want is not one you can force into being. Two streams meeting is a choice both make, and wanting it harder will not make the other side go faster. What you are after comes from tending, not from gripping. What you put in is already growing, and the work now is to let it, which is a different skill than the one that got you here.
cells.sheetLine: You are pushing the future into the room before it is ready to be here.

cells.tense: You stopped moving when something did not go the way you needed it to, and you have been standing at that door since.
cells.ask: Put one thing you want in front of one person this week — imperfectly, without preparing it first.
cells.core: Going well, this seat looks like a pull you can follow without checking first — you notice a direction, you take a step, the step answers back, and you adjust. That loop is what makes the aim trustworthy, because reality gets a vote in it early and often.\n\nRight now the loop is stopped. You know the direction — you have known — but something back there made moving feel unsafe, and you have been quiet since. Not numb. Just not arriving. What is missing is not desire. It is your own read on what is real and what is not, and that is the part that needs feeding, not more effort in the direction itself. Show one thing to one person before you are sure of it, and let what comes back tell you which way to go.
cells.sheetLine: You know the direction and you have stopped moving toward it.

cells.tense: You are already steering by this pull — it shapes what you notice, what you move toward, what you let go — and you talk about it as if it were just how things are.
cells.ask: Say 'I chose this' about one direction you have been describing as just where things led.
cells.core: The pull is running and you are following it, but the account you give is that it happened to you. You describe the direction as obvious, or as where things led, or as what anyone would do. You made the call and you are not saying so.\n\nThat matters because a direction you have not owned is one you cannot really refine. You cannot tend what you will not admit you are growing. The recovery is not a new plan — it is returning to a smaller, simpler form of the same thing: one place where you say plainly that this is what you want and you are the one going after it. Not the whole life. One thing.

The sentence that serves the writer is 'you've been walking toward this on purpose' — cut it.
